mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that triggers corporate cost-cutting and reduced capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and residential sales (HOUST and RSAFS) indicates a contraction in the housing sector, which reduces consumer wealth and business investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply chain disruption regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced manufacturing output, which increases corporate input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during supply chain disruptions when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past month indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in unemployment rate (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling) signals a tight monetary policy coinciding with a strong labor market, which increases corporate borrowing costs without sufficient wage growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the interaction term in a regression model is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-recession recovery regime, a rising residential sales index (RSAFS) indicates improving consumer confidence and housing market activity, which boosts retail sales and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during post-recession recovery when RSAFS rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
